patch.description: Changes dates, room type, occupancy or notes. Inventory is re-allocated in the same transaction: the new dates are claimed before the old ones are released, so a modification that cannot be satisfied returns 409 SOLD_OUT and leaves the original booking intact. A pre-assigned room that no longer fits is dropped. Not permitted once the guest is in house — use room-move or extend instead.

post.description: Assigns a specific room, or picks one automatically when `roomId` is omitted. Auto-assignment prefers the lowest floor and skips rooms that are blocked, out of order, or already assigned to an overlapping stay.

404.description: ROOM_NOT_FOUND — unknown room, or not of this reservation's type

get.description: Confirmed stays arriving on the business date, each with the blockers stopping check-in.
In-house stays departing on the business date, with per-folio balances and whether checkout is clear.
Every currently in-house stay.
Counts for arrivals, departures and in-house, plus total outstanding on departing folios.

post.summary: Open an additional folio on a stay
post.description: Splits billing, e.g. room and tax to a company account and extras to the guest. Max six per stay.

Moves postings between folios of the SAME stay. The ledger is append-only, so nothing is re-parented: each entry is reversed on the source and re-posted on the target, both halves sharing a transferGroupId. The pair is exactly zero-sum. An entry can only be transferred once.

get.description: Every folio on a stay with its balance — the checkout screen's data.
Issued documents for a property, newest first.

post.description: Freezes an immutable snapshot of the folio's current lines, taxes and guest details and assigns the next gapless number in the property's yearly series. Later postings to the folio never alter an issued document.

get.description: Returns the frozen snapshot.
Plain-text rendering sized for the thermal printers front desks actually own.

post.description: Issues an offsetting credit note and marks the original VOID. The original keeps its number — a gapless sequence must never lose an entry. Finance, manager or owner only.

get.description: Reports whether each adapter is LIVE or SANDBOX and what that means. Live mode requires PAYMENTS_MODE=live plus credentials — it is never inferred from the shape of a key.

post.description: Creates a local record and a provider checkout URL. Nothing touches the folio: money is only posted from a verified webhook or an explicit verify call, because a browser redirect proves nothing.

201.description: Intent created; returns checkoutUrl and a sandbox flag

post.description: Asks the provider directly whether the transaction succeeded. Used when a webhook is delayed or lost. Idempotent: confirming twice creates one payment.

Signature-verified provider callback. Paystack: HMAC-SHA512 of the RAW body in x-paystack-signature. Flutterwave: shared secret echoed in verif-hash.

Verification runs over the exact received bytes — a re-serialised body will not validate. Every delivery is stored before being acted on, deduplicated by provider event id, and replays are no-ops. Returns 2xx for business-level problems (unknown reference, duplicate) because a non-2xx makes providers retry forever; only a bad signature returns 4xx.

201.description: Accepted (may be duplicate, ignored or unmatched)

get.description: Refund requests, newest first.

post.description: Raises a refund for approval. Nothing is posted to the ledger until a different, authorised user approves it. Cannot exceed what remains unrefunded on the payment.
Finance, manager or owner only. The requester can never approve their own request. Approval posts a REFUND entry to the folio and, for card payments, calls the provider.
Finance, manager or owner only. The requester can never approve their own request. Approval posts a REFUND entry to the folio and, for card payments, calls the provider.
Imports a payout and reconciles it against recorded payments. Idempotent on the payout reference. Anything that does not reconcile becomes an exception rather than a silent adjustment.

201.description: Imported; returns matched count and exceptions

get.description: Payouts with gross, fees, net and exception counts.
MISSING_IN_SETTLEMENT (we recorded it, the provider did not pay it), UNKNOWN_IN_SETTLEMENT (they paid something we never recorded), AMOUNT_MISMATCH, DUPLICATE_REFERENCE.

post.description: Finance, manager or owner only. Requires a note; exceptions are worked, never auto-cleared.

post.summary: Import a settlement from a provider CSV
post.description:
Parses a Paystack or Flutterwave settlement export and reconciles it through the same path as the JSON import.

Amounts in these exports are in MAJOR units (naira) even where the provider's API uses minor units, so they are converted explicitly. Column lookup is case- and punctuation-insensitive with known aliases. Unreadable rows are reported with their row numbers rather than dropped; `strict` refuses the whole import if any row failed.

201.description: Imported; returns matched count, exceptions and parse report

get.description: Reports whether the day can close. Blockers stop the run (open cashier shifts, open POS orders, already run); warnings must be acknowledged but do not stop it (unapproved variances, due-outs still in house, unarrived bookings).
Reports the active adapter, whether it is a real object store, bucket policy, size limits and allowed content types.

post.description: Validates purpose, content type and size, reserves a metadata row and returns a presigned PUT. The row exists before the bytes do, so an abandoned upload is visible and sweepable rather than an orphan. Object keys are generated — the uploaded filename is never used as a path component.

201.description: Intent created with a presigned upload

post.description: Accepts raw bytes for a presigned URL. Public because the signature and expiry ARE the authorisation. Rejects tampered or expired URLs and refuses a second upload to the same key.

Verifies size and checksum, then sniffs the stored bytes. A declared content type is only a hint: a mismatch quarantines the file, which is what stops an HTML payload being stored as an image and served back. Idempotent once CLEAN.

get.description: Short-lived signed URL for private objects; public-bucket objects are returned unsigned. Quarantined, deleted or incomplete files are never served.

Verifies the signature and expiry, then re-checks the metadata row: a valid signature alone is not enough, because the row is the authority on whether bytes may still be served. Always sent as an attachment with nosniff.
Filter by attached entity or status.

post.description: Manual quarantine. Requires the file.manage permission.
Marks the file deleted. Previously issued download URLs stop working immediately; the bytes are purged by the lifecycle sweep while the metadata row is kept for audit.

Expires abandoned intents, purges soft-deleted objects and enforces retention (identity documents are kept far more briefly than room images). Metadata rows survive so a deletion can still be explained.

get.description:
Emits change notifications, never payloads: a client is told what changed and re-reads through the normal permission-checked endpoints, so authorisation lives in exactly one place.

EventSource cannot set an Authorization header, so the access token is passed as a query parameter and verified with the same secret; the connection is scoped to the tenant in that verified token. Frames: `ready` on connect, `change` per event, and comment heartbeats every 20s so intermediaries do not close an idle connection. `retry: 5000` tells the browser how long to wait before reconnecting.
Reports whether VAPID keys are configured and returns the public key. When push is off it says so plainly rather than accepting subscriptions that can never deliver.

post.description: Upserts on the endpoint, so re-subscribing the same browser updates the row instead of accumulating duplicates that would double-notify.
Removes the subscription for this user.

get.description: Devices this user has registered.

post.description: Lets a user prove push works on this device before relying on it. Returns per-device outcomes: sent, failed and pruned.

Assigns the task and queues a push notification in the SAME transaction, so nobody is told to clean a room for an assignment that rolled back. Bumps the version so offline devices see the reassignment. The assignee must be an active member of the tenant.

get.description: Active catalogue for a property.

post.description: Quantities are held as integers in thousandths so 0.1 + 0.2 is exactly 0.3 - a float ledger drifts, and a drifting stock ledger cannot distinguish rounding from theft.

Append-only: a mistake is corrected with an opposing ADJUSTMENT, never an edit, so shrinkage cannot be quietly erased. Send a POSITIVE quantity - the type decides the sign. Stock cannot be driven negative, because a location holding -3 bottles hides either an unrecorded delivery or a theft.

get.description: Current levels with valuation and reorder flags.
Consumption and wastage over a period. Wastage is reported in its own column rather than folded into consumption.
Every movement for one item with a running balance.

ADR divides room revenue by rooms SOLD; RevPAR divides the same revenue by rooms AVAILABLE. Confusing the two flatters a half-empty hotel, so both denominators are returned alongside the rates. Blocked rooms reduce availability.
Payments and refunds are excluded: they settle revenue, they are not revenue. Tax and discounts are reported separately from gross.
Shifts with expected vs counted. Shortages and overages are totalled SEPARATELY - netting them hides two different problems behind one number.
Open balances bucketed by age. Folios that are CLOSED but still owing are counted separately: that is a debt that walked out of the building.
Month-to-date occupancy/ADR/RevPAR, receivables ageing, and a needs-attention block covering pending approvals, unapproved cash variances and open reconciliation exceptions.

post.description: A year of guest ledger will not return inside an HTTP request, so the job is recorded, run out of band, and the result stored as a file downloaded through a signed URL. Poll the job for status. Every type in the enum has a builder behind it; a type without one fails the job with a reason rather than returning an empty file that reads like a quiet trading period. PDF output is A4 landscape, fixed pitch, paginated and numbered; the naira sign is written NGN because it has no WinAnsi code point. CSV and PDF of the same report always carry the same columns.

get.description: Returns status, row count and - once COMPLETE - a signed download URL.

post.summary: Void an order (approval above the correction window)
post.description: A void is the one POS action that makes revenue disappear, which makes it the obvious way to take cash from a till: ring the order, collect, void the ticket, keep the difference. Small voids (at or under NGN5,000) caught within 15 minutes of the order opening are treated as keying corrections and apply immediately. Anything larger or older parks the order in VOID_PENDING and raises a POS_VOID approval request; the order can then be neither settled nor voided again until a different user with approval.decide decides it. Approval voids the order; rejection returns it to OPEN and clears the reason, so a live ticket never looks cancelled. Holders of approval.decide void directly - their name is on the audit entry, which is where the control actually rests. A SETTLED order is never voidable: reverse the folio entry or refund.

201.description: VOIDED, or PENDING_APPROVAL with the raised request
